content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain white roll is a soft bun made from whole‑grain wheat flour, baked without artificial colourings. It has a mild taste, a light bread aroma and a slightly sweet aftertaste. The roll is commonly used as a base for sandwiches, snacks and breakfasts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain flour retains the bran and germ, making the product more nutritious than refined white flour.
The white colour of the roll is achieved by using only wheat flour without added seeds or grains.
Traditionally popular in European cuisine, these rolls are often served with butter, cheese or ham.
Baked whole‑grain products have a longer shelf life due to lower moisture content.
Rolls are frequently chosen for diet plans because the fibre provides a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Rich in dietary fibre
items.content: Whole‑grain rolls contain fibre that supports normal bowel function and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They provide thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which are essential for metabolism and energy production.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The roll supplies iron, magnesium and zinc, important for blood formation and immune health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white bread, whole‑grain rolls raise blood sugar more slowly.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fibre and plant phytochemicals help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with gluten intolerance or wheat allergy may experience adverse reactions when consuming the roll.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some roll varieties contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although less calorie‑dense than white bread, overeating can still lead to excess energy intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the roll fresh, split it open and spread butter, cream cheese or hummus. It works well for sandwiches with turkey, vegetables and greens, and makes a convenient breakfast base.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze them wrapped in plastic to prevent drying out.
